title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Polynomial Decomposition, Discrete Tomography Switch, and Legendre Cross-Polytope Coupling Certificates
abstract: Peter Keevash and Jeck Lim (arXiv:2611.33120, November 24, 2026) proved a sharp linear-overhead polynomial decomposition theorem (Theorem 1.2) enabling absorption and approximate counting for planar lattice configurations with multi-direction X-ray constraints, anchored by a miraculous signed cross-polytope coupling defined via Legendre polynomials Q(x) = L_{k-1}(||x||_1) (Theorem 1.6). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and symbolic exact-Z/Q certificate auditor for the finite algebraic and coupling core of this work. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 3 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes 2D/3D basic switches, (1-x^m) evaluation vanishing on List Int, X-ray determinant shift and parallel invisibility, Section 1.3 Gram-zero uniqueness (sum p_i^2 = 0 -> all p_i = 0), Legendre normalisation/parity/orthogonality, Theorem 1.6's exact k=2 r^2-cancellation (1-r^2)+r(r-s)=1-rs, and inductive filling-norm bounds. POLY-RECONFIG-CERT-1.0 audits four exact modes—including symbolic Q[r,s] integration of all four pieces T1+T2+T3+T4 of Theorem 1.6 up to k=5—replaying 16 canonical certificates in 0.056-6.095 ms, verifying all 15/15 pairs (k,l) (1 <= k <= 5), and rejecting 57/57 live adversarial forgeries.
